background_definition.rule: Both nominal baseline measures strictly below separate weighted cutoffs
background_definition.reference_population: Selected panel, each respondent counted once

variables.female: 1 for sex code 2; 0 for sex code 1
variables.college: 1 for highest-degree codes 4-7 by the 2015 interview; otherwise 0
variables.age: Earnings calendar year minus birth year (year-end age)
variables.custom_weight: Stored custom weight / 100 (two implied decimal places)
variables.regression_weight: Custom weight divided by the person-level sample mean
variables.household_net_worth_2025: 1997 household net worth times CPI_2025 / CPI_1997
variables.low_background: Indicator for both baseline resources strictly below their weighted cutoffs

caveats: The default 60th-percentile definition is inherited from an exploratory cutoff search; it is not a preregistered definition.
Both resources must be strictly below their separate cutoffs. The comparison group is all other backgrounds, not uniformly wealthy respondents.
The cleaned sample excludes valid skips and requires three observed earnings amounts. Receipt filters are absent, so skipped amounts have not been recoded as zeros.
Custom weights belong to the selected sample. New sample membership requires compatible weights and renewed sample validation.
ASVAB_MATH_VERBAL_SCORE_PCT already normalizes within three-month birth groups; division by 1000 restores stored units.
Degree status is fixed at the 2015 interview; no BA does not mean never attended college.
The 2025 CPI mean uses 11 supplied months: October is absent; no month is imputed.
